title: Motion Equations for Constant Acceleration in One Dimension
lead: When acceleration is constant, a small set of equations relates displacement, velocity, acceleration, and time. This section derives those equations and shows how to choose the one that fits a given problem.
objectives: Calculate displacement of an object that is not accelerating, given initial position and velocity.
Calculate final velocity of an accelerating object, given initial velocity, acceleration, and time.
Calculate displacement and final position of an accelerating object, given initial position, initial velocity, time, and acceleration.
summary_html:
• To simplify calculations we take acceleration to be constant, so that $\kab = \ka$ at all times.
  • We also take initial time to be zero.
  • Initial position and velocity are given a subscript 0; final values have no subscript. Thus, $\kdt = \kt$, $\kdx = \kx - \kxo$, $\kdv = \kv - \kvo$.
  • The following kinematic equations for motion with constant $\ka$ are useful: $\kx = \kxo + \kvb\kt$, $\kvb = \frac{\kvo + \kv}{2}$, $\kv = \kvo + \ka\kt$, $\kx = \kxo + \kvo\kt + \tfrac{1}{2}\ka\kt^2$, $\kv^2 = \kvo^2 + 2\ka(\kx - \kxo)$.
  • In vertical motion, $y$ is substituted for $\kx$.
